Beautiful Tiny House Pours French Sparkle Over Self-Sufficient Living
26 photos
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois
“Open Air” is a beautiful and wonderfully fitting name for a tiny house on wheels designed to turn the joy of being outdoors into a way of living. Equipped for a comfortable off-grid lifestyle, tiny house Plein Air adds that lovely French touch that makes even the humblest mobile abode seem like a piece of fairytale.
A wood-burning fireplace, mysterious timber shutters at all the windows, and the aroma of natural wood, inside and out – this is, in a nutshell, the formula of an enchanting homely ambiance. The builder of tiny house Plein Air, Mon Reve en Bois, describes it poetically as “happiness all year round”, and what could be better than that? This perfect, wholesome happiness comes from reliable autonomy, enhanced comfort, and harmony with nature.
Tiny house Plein Air is French in every way, yet it offers beautiful volume throughout, and one of the best layouts by all standards, simply thanks to a bigger size. Legally, this spacious home is still designed as a tiny house approved for the road, but everything about it was thought out for long-term accommodation, settled somewhere in a beautiful environment. The builder presents it as one of their best models for couples and even family living.
This generous volume, carefully organized into one of the most efficient layouts, comes from a length of 8.5 meters (27.8 feet), a 3-meter (9.8 feet) width, and an exterior height of slightly over four meters (13 feet). In total, Tiny Plein Air offers 34.5 square meters (372 square feet) of floor space, considerably more than the average French tiny house.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Although the single loft in this configuration is the only formal bedroom, Tiny Plein Air can accommodate up to four people thanks to a lovely, big lounge that can double as a second room. It also boasts a charming L-shaped kitchen that takes up one end of the house, and a fully-equipped bathroom (nestled right next to the kitchen).
This configuration sounds basic, yet the added spaciousness for each living space inside this tiny house allows for greater versatility which, in turn, improves functionality beyond what is typically attainable in a regular 6-meter home on wheels built in France. For instance, the open lounge can be much more than a simple space for relaxation. A pop-up tabletop, made of pure timber, turns this area into a dining room.
Looking almost invisible when folded, this pop-up table located near the main entrance, makes room for at least four seats. Plus, additional tables and chairs can make their way closer to the sofa, allowing for even more dining options. Resting against the wall, the lounge sofa combines comfy seating with built-in storage. The free floor space in this part of the house is like an open invitation for a workspace, hobbies, yoga, and many more.
A lot more is possible thanks to the residential-style separation between the lounge and the kitchen. In compact homes on wheels, these two areas are often intertwined. Tiny Plein Air, however, places each one at a separate end, which allows full functionality and also frees up a large section of floor space in the transition area between them. When it comes to tiny living, every extra inch of free floor space equals luxury.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Large windows help make this spacious tiny house seem even bigger by flooding it with natural light. Two windows in the lounge, two windows in the kitchen area, and two windows in the loft bedroom – there’s no scarcity when it comes to natural light and fresh air (the bathroom, of course, has its own window as well).
The L-shaped kitchen is one of the most unique features of Tiny Plein Air. Its placement is unusual (most of the times, kitchens are found in the center, with the lounge at one end and the bathroom at the other end), and the L-shaped design translates to a more generous counter surface and better storage compared to the usual compact kitchens. Those who appreciate the quality of natural timber will also love the beautiful bespoke cabinetry.
There are no upper cupboards at all, which results in a brighter and airier cooking space, especially with those two large windows bringing in extra light. Bespoke cabinets offer sufficient storage, including separate nooks for appliances.
Additional storage is available in the staircase located between the bathroom and the lounge. Custom-crafted like the rest of the furniture, it turns only a few treads into hidden drawers, and also features a larger cabinet built into it. It’s not the crazy built-in storage you see in other staircases, with tens of drawers and cabinets throughout, but it enhances the home’s storage capacity in an elegant, more discrete way, that doesn’t clash with the airy interior.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois The staircase leads to a deliciously spacious loft bedroom, far better than what many French tiny homes offer. Even with a standard double bed, there’s ample walk-around space. Built-in cabinets at the head of the bed match the minimalist nightstands. Large windows on each side keep the air circulating while adding the luxury of glorious views.
The version of Tiny Plein Air pictured in the gallery comes with a complete off-grid kit, including everything from solar power to water tanks, and water filtration systems. The wood-burning fireplace sitting in a dedicated, insulated corner of the lounge is not just for fun – it’s actually the only source of heat for this self-sufficient abode. The same goes for the toilet, which may look rustic, but is in fact a waterless design meant to save water and energy.
Like all the models from this French builder based in Occitania, Tiny Plein Air is a living tribute to the beauty of raw timber, inside and out. This builder prides itself in only using certified timber obtained from sustainably-managed local woods in Occitania – a practice that supports local craftsmanship and this priceless natural resource.
Self-sufficient, but not rugged to the point where it feels uninviting – this French tiny house knows how to sprinkle the special magic that makes any plain house feel like home. The traditional aesthetic that might seem too rustic for some is, in fact, what minimalism in harmony with nature should look like. There’s absolutely nothing artificial, cheap, or cookie-cutter about this lovely interior, and this actually makes it more luxurious than an expensive mansion.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois This is the kind of luxury that isn’t reflected in the price tag. The fully-equipped version pictured in the gallery, complete with a full autonomy kit, is valued at under €70,000 ($77,000). The only downside is that French tiny homes are available exclusively in France. As small companies and artisan workshops, most tiny house builders in this country deliver only locally or throughout France, at best.
Still, such a beautiful tiny house like Plein Air, from its perfect layout to the craftsmanship quality, can become a rich source of inspiration for anyone in search of their dream tiny homes. The world of tiny house design is much more versatile than many people think, from the most traditional perspective to radical contemporary style.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Tiny house Plein Air is proof that you don’t necessarily need an XL tiny house for comfortable tiny living, and also that an all-wood home on wheels can be just as cozy and functional as its more modern counterparts.
